readings.title: The Law of the Guilt Offering
readings.subtitle: Priestly Portions and Procedures
readings.text: [Leviticus 7:1] <dq>‘And this is the Torah of the guilt offering: It is most set-apart.</dq> [2] <dq>‘In the place where they slaughter <dn>את</dn> the burnt offering, they slaughter <dn>את</dn> the guilt offering. And <dn>את</dn> its blood he sprinkles on the altar all around.</dq> [3] <dq>‘And he brings near from it <dn>את</dn> all its fat: <dn>את</dn> the fat tail and <dn>את</dn> the fat that covers the entrails,</dq> [4] <dq>and <dn>את</dn> the two kidneys and <dn>את</dn> the fat that is on them by the loins, and <dn>את</dn> the appendage on the liver, which he removes with the kidneys.</dq> [5] <dq>‘And the priest shall burn <dn>את</dn> them on the altar as an offering made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. It is a guilt offering.</dq> [6] <dq>‘Every male among the priests eats <dn>את</dn> it. It is eaten in a set-apart place. It is most set-apart.</dq> [7] <dq>‘The guilt offering is like the sin offering, there is one Torah for them both: the priest who makes atonement with it, it is his.</dq> [8] <dq>‘And the priest who brings near <dn>את</dn> any man’s burnt offering, the skin of the burnt offering which he has brought near is the priest’s, it is his.</dq> [9] <dq>‘And every grain offering that is baked in the oven, and all that is prepared in the stewing-pot, or on a griddle, belongs to the priest who brings it near, it is his.</dq> [10] <dq>‘And every grain offering, mixed with oil or dry, belongs to all the sons of Aharon, to one as much as the other.</dq>

readings.title: The Law of the Peace Offering
readings.subtitle: Thanksgiving and Vow Offerings
readings.text: [Leviticus 7:11] <dq>‘And this is the Torah of the slaughtering of peace offerings which is brought to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>:</dq> [12] <dq>‘If he brings it for a thanksgiving, then he shall bring with the slaughtering of thanksgiving unleavened cakes mixed with oil, and unleavened thin cakes anointed with oil, or cakes of finely blended flour mixed with oil.</dq> [13] <dq>‘With the cakes of leavened bread he brings <dn>את</dn> his offering with the slaughtering of his peace offering for thanksgiving.</dq> [14] <dq>‘And from it he shall bring one cake from each offering as a contribution to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. It belongs to the priest who sprinkles the blood of the peace offering.</dq> [15] <dq>‘And the flesh of the slaughtering of his peace offering for thanksgiving is eaten the same day it is offered. He does not leave any of it until morning.</dq> [16] <dq>‘And if the offering he brings is a vow or a voluntary offering, it is eaten the same day that he brings his slaughtering, and what is left of it is eaten the next day.</dq> [17] <dq>‘But what is left of the flesh of the slaughtering on the third day is burned with fire.</dq> [18] <dq>‘And if any of the flesh of the slaughtering of his peace offering is eaten at all on the third day, it is not accepted. It is not reckoned to him who brings it, it is refuse, and the being who eats of it bears his perversity.</dq> [19] <dq>‘And the flesh that touches any unclean thing is not eaten, it is burned with fire. And as for the clean flesh, all who are clean eat of it.</dq> [20] <dq>‘But the being who eats the flesh of the slaughtering of peace offerings that belongs to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, while he is unclean, that being shall be cut off from his people.</dq> [21] <dq>‘And when a being touches any unclean thing, the uncleanness of man, or an unclean beast, or any unclean abomination, and eats the flesh of the slaughtering of the peace offering that belongs to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, that being shall be cut off from his people.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: Prohibition Against Eating Fat and Blood
readings.subtitle: Set-apart Portions for YeHoVaH
readings.text: [Leviticus 7:22] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [23] <dq>“Speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, saying, ‘Do not eat any fat, of bull or sheep or goat.</dq> [24] <dq>‘And the fat of a dead body, and the fat of what is torn, is used for any purpose, but you do not eat it at all.</dq> [25] <dq>‘For whoever eats the fat of the beast of which men bring an offering made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, even the being who eats it shall be cut off from his people.</dq> [26] <dq>‘And do not eat any blood in any of your dwellings, of bird or of beast.</dq> [27] <dq>‘Any being who eats any blood, even that being shall be cut off from his people.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: The Portion of the Priests
readings.subtitle: The Wave Breast and Heave Thigh
readings.text: [Leviticus 7:28] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [29] <dq>“Speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, saying, ‘He who brings his slaughtering of peace offerings to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> brings <dn>את</dn> his offering to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> from the slaughtering of his peace offerings.</dq> [30] <dq>‘His own hands bring <dn>את</dn> the offerings made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. He brings <dn>את</dn> the fat with the breast, so that <dn>את</dn> the breast is waved as a wave offering before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [31] <dq>‘And the priest shall burn <dn>את</dn> the fat on the altar, but the breast shall be Aharon’s and his sons’.</dq> [32] <dq>‘And <dn>את</dn> the right thigh you give to the priest as a contribution from the slaughtering of your peace offerings.</dq> [33] <dq>‘He among the sons of Aharon, who brings <dn>את</dn> the blood of the peace offerings and <dn>את</dn> the fat, the right thigh is his for a portion.</dq> [34] <dq>‘For <dn>את</dn> the breast of the wave offering and <dn>את</dn> the thigh of the contribution <dn>I</dn> have taken from the children of Yisra’ĕl, from the slaughtering of their peace offerings, and I give <dn>את</dn> them to Aharon the priest and to his sons, as a law forever, from the children of Yisra’ĕl.’ ”</dq> [35] This is the anointed portion for Aharon and the anointed portion for his sons, from the offerings made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, on the day when Mosheh brought them to serve as priests to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, [36] which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded to be given to them by the children of Yisra’ĕl, on the day that <dn>He</dn> anointed <dn>את</dn> them – a law forever throughout their generations. [37] This is the Torah of the burnt offering, of the grain offering, and of the sin offering, and of the guilt offering, and of the ordinations, and of the slaughtering of peace offerings, [38] which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded <dn>את</dn> Mosheh on Mount Sinai, on the day when <dn>He</dn> commanded the children of Yisra’ĕl to bring <dn>את</dn> their offerings to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> in the Wilderness of Sinai.

readings.title: The Consecration of the Priests
readings.subtitle: Aharon and His Sons Set Apart
readings.text: [Leviticus 8:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [2] <dq>“Take <dn>את</dn> Aharon and <dn>את</dn> his sons with him, and <dn>את</dn> the garments, and <dn>את</dn> the anointing oil, and <dn>את</dn> the bull for the sin offering, and <dn>את</dn> the two rams, and <dn>את</dn> the basket of unleavened bread,</dq> [3] <dq>and assemble <dn>את</dn> all the congregation at the door of the Tent of Meeting.”</dq> [4] And Mosheh did as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded <dn>את</dn> him, and the congregation was assembled at the door of the Tent of Meeting. [5] And Mosheh said to the congregation, “This is the word which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded to be done.” [6] And Mosheh brought <dn>את</dn> Aharon and <dn>את</dn> his sons and washed <dn>את</dn> them with water. [7] And he put on him <dn>את</dn> the long shirt, and girded <dn>את</dn> him with the girdle, and dressed <dn>את</dn> him in <dn>את</dn> the robe, and put on him <dn>את</dn> the shoulder garment, and girded <dn>את</dn> him with the embroidered band of the shoulder garment, and with it bound to him <dn>את</dn> the shoulder garment. [8] And he put on him <dn>את</dn> the breastplate, and he put in the breastplate <dn>את</dn> the Urim and <dn>את</dn> the Tummim. [9] And he put <dn>את</dn> the turban on his head. And on the turban, on his forehead, he put <dn>את</dn> the golden plate, the set-apart sign of dedication, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded <dn>את</dn> Mosheh. [10] And Mosheh took <dn>את</dn> the anointing oil, and anointed <dn>את</dn> the Dwelling Place and <dn>את</dn> all that was in it, and set <dn>את</dn> them apart. [11] And he sprinkled some of it on the altar seven times, and anointed <dn>את</dn> the altar and <dn>את</dn> all its utensils, and <dn>את</dn> the basin and <dn>את</dn> its stand, to set them apart. [12] And he poured some of the anointing oil on Aharon’s head and anointed <dn>את</dn> him, to set him apart. [13] And Mosheh brought <dn>את</dn> the sons of Aharon and put long shirts on them, and girded <dn>את</dn> them with girdles, and put turbans on them, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded <dn>את</dn> Mosheh. [14] And he brought <dn>את</dn> the bull for the sin offering. And Aharon and his sons laid <dn>את</dn> their hands on the head of the bull for the sin offering, [15] and it was slaughtered. And Mosheh took <dn>את</dn> the blood, and put some on the horns of the altar all around with his finger, and cleansed <dn>את</dn> the altar. And <dn>את</dn> the blood he poured at the base of the altar, and set <dn>את</dn> it apart, to make atonement for it. [16] And he took <dn>את</dn> all the fat that was on the entrails, and <dn>את</dn> the appendage on the liver, and <dn>את</dn> the two kidneys with their fat, and Mosheh burned them on the altar. [17] But <dn>את</dn> the bull, and <dn>את</dn> its skin, and <dn>את</dn> its flesh, and <dn>את</dn> its dung, he burned with fire outside the camp, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded <dn>את</dn> Mosheh. [18] And he brought <dn>את</dn> the ram of the burnt offering. And Aharon and his sons laid <dn>את</dn> their hands on the head of the ram, [19] and it was slaughtered. And Mosheh sprinkled <dn>את</dn> the blood on the altar all around. [20] And the ram was cut into its pieces. And Mosheh burned <dn>את</dn> the head, and <dn>את</dn> the pieces, and <dn>את</dn> the fat. [21] And <dn>את</dn> the entrails and <dn>את</dn> the legs he washed with water. And Mosheh burned <dn>את</dn> the entire ram on the altar. It was a burnt offering for a sweet fragrance, an offering made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded <dn>את</dn> Mosheh. [22] And he brought <dn>את</dn> the second ram, the ram of ordination. And Aharon and his sons laid <dn>את</dn> their hands on the head of the ram, [23] and it was slaughtered. And Mosheh took some of its blood and put it on the tip of Aharon’s right ear, and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot. [24] And he brought <dn>את</dn> Aharon’s sons. And Mosheh put some of the blood on the tips of their right ears, and on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet. And Mosheh sprinkled <dn>את</dn> the blood on the altar all around. [25] And he took <dn>את</dn> the fat and <dn>את</dn> the fat tail, and <dn>את</dn> all the fat that was on the entrails, and <dn>את</dn> the appendage on the liver, and <dn>את</dn> the two kidneys and <dn>את</dn> their fat, and <dn>את</dn> the right thigh. [26] And from the basket of unleavened bread that was before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> he took one unleavened cake, and a cake of bread anointed with oil, and one thin cake, and put them on the fat and on the right thigh, [27] and placed <dn>את</dn> all of them in the hands of Aharon and in the hands of his sons, and waved <dn>את</dn> them as a wave offering before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [28] Then Mosheh took <dn>את</dn> them from their hands and burned them on the altar, on the burnt offering. They were ordinations for a sweet fragrance. It was an offering made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [29] And Mosheh took <dn>את</dn> the breast and waved <dn>את</dn> it as a wave offering before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. It was Mosheh’s portion of the ram of ordination, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded <dn>את</dn> Mosheh. [30] And Mosheh took some of the anointing oil and some of the blood which was on the altar, and sprinkled it on Aharon, on his garments, and on his sons, and on the garments of his sons with him. And he set apart <dn>את</dn> Aharon, <dn>את</dn> his garments, and <dn>את</dn> his sons, and <dn>את</dn> the garments of his sons with him. [31] And Mosheh said to Aharon and his sons, “Boil <dn>את</dn> the flesh at the door of the Tent of Meeting, and eat <dn>את</dn> it there with the bread that is in the basket of ordinations, as I commanded, saying, ‘Aharon and his sons eat <dn>את</dn> it.’ [32] “And what is left of the flesh and of the bread you burn with fire. [33] “And do not go outside the door of the Tent of Meeting for seven days, until the days of your ordination are completed. For he fills <dn>את</dn> your hands for seven days. [34] “As has been done this day, so <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has commanded to do, to make atonement for you. [35] “And stay at the door of the Tent of Meeting day and night for seven days, and guard <dn>את</dn> the duty of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and not die, for so I have been commanded.” [36] And Aharon and his sons did <dn>את</dn> all the matters which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded by the hand of Mosheh.
